calls.head: The Golden Knights’ power play has a target
calls.body: The Golden Knights’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Canucks’ kill is one of the league’s worst. The Canucks need to stay out of the box.
calls.call: The Golden Knights’ power play creates at least their usual 8.7 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: Vegas 3rd for power play (8.7 expected goals per 60) · Vancouver 28th for penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: Vegas’s power play created 13.0 expected goals per 60 in 7:53 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 8.7, and scored 1 goal.
calls.beyond: Vegas’s power play created 13.0 expected goals per 60, against their usual 8.7 and a league average of 7.5. A team strays this far about once every 8 games.

calls.head: The Golden Knights should pile up the shots
calls.body: The Golden Knights shoot a lot, and the Canucks are the league’s worst at keeping shots down. Look for a big shot total.
calls.call: The Golden Knights take at least their usual 59.5 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.nums: Vegas 9th for shot volume (59.5 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Vancouver 32nd for shot suppression
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: Vegas took 56.9 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against their usual 59.5.

VAN.head: We gave Vancouver only a 18% chance, and it went the way we feared.

VGK.head: We gave Vegas a 82% chance, and Vegas delivered.

surprises.head: Vegas got the good looks
surprises.body: Vegas’s shots at 5-on-5 were more dangerous than usual: an 11.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 400 games.

surprises.head: Vegas shut down Vancouver’s power play
surprises.body: Vancouver’s power play created 2.8 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.2 and a league average of 7.5. A team strays this far about once every 10 games.

story.head: The Golden Knights beat the Canucks
paras: Paul Cotter opened the scoring late in the first. The game was tied twice. Marc Gatcomb scored the winner late in the second.
The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Golden Knights win nine in ten.

items.text: One of the preview’s two calls held.
